steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Urbanisation is the increase in the proportion of people living in urban areas (towns and cities) compared to rural areas (countryside). It is caused by rural-urban migration and natural increase within cities.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: HICs (High-Income Countries) are already highly urbanised (over 75%). The fastest urbanisation is happening in LICs (Low-Income Countries) and NEEs (Newly Emerging Economies), where rates of urban growth can exceed 4% per year.

steps.title: Key Concept
steps.body: Rural-urban migration is driven by push factors (negative conditions that drive people away from rural areas) and pull factors (positive attractions that draw people to cities). People weigh up both sets of factors when deciding to move.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Natural increase is the growth of the urban population through births exceeding deaths. It accounts for roughly 60% of urban growth in LICs and NEEs, with migration accounting for the remaining 40%.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always define urbanisation before discussing its causes or impacts Use specific facts and statistics for megacities (population, growth rates) For push-pull questions, give equal attention to both sets of factors Know the difference between migration and natural increase as causes of urban growth Explain that natural increase and migration are INTERLINKED, not separate Use LIC/NEE examples for megacities - examiners expect Dhaka, Lagos, Mumbai
